title: SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions
main_claim: Take any small square-symmetric finite-range contour potential U with |lambda| < lambda_0(J,U), of either sign. There is then a domain-independent inverse temperature beta_c(J,U,lambda), analytic in lambda with beta_c(0) = log(1+sqrt2)/(2J), at which the Dobrushin spin interface converges to chordal SLE_3 in the full oriented curve metric. This holds for arbitrary admissible exterior contours and for Jordan domains approximated uniformly in boundary parametrization.

issues.location: Sec. 2 (02-pure-inputs.tex), Props. pure-buffered, signed-transmission, line-continuity, Thm. pure-cle
issues.description: The argument depends on companion-paper inputs that are imported, not proved here: buffered pointwise comparison with arbitrary common pins, the ordered-source transmission inequality with exponent -7/8+eta, nearby-line prediction, and the 'every complete resolution' extension of the CLE_3 convergence. The hypotheses as quoted match how they are used (an order-positive centered source, pin-free admissible cuts, and the fixed ratio taken before the mesh limit). This audit does not re-verify them. The sibling review of the companion paper (rank 53) reported no gap.
issues.evidence: "We cite three equilibrium estimates and one complete-resolution result from the companion article ... We use these results as pure-model inputs"

coverage:
I read all seven sections of build/sections in full. Section 4 had both halves read; the proofs of Sections 2 and 5 were read in full apart from the opening of the line-sum material. Checks:
- Lemma contour-spin: the bijection, the parity argument for the arc signs, and why exterior stubs cannot sit at reflex corners.
- Sec. 3: the window/HS lemma; the Gaussian-observation smoothing, including order-positivity from conditional FKG, <z,a> >= ||z||^2, and the exponent bookkeeping n^{-7/8+eta}/n^{-3/8} giving a sum of n^{2 eta}; the overlap moment and exponential-projection identity; the bounded replacement lemma; radial reflection positivity and the semigroup; the r-expansion and the r^2 coefficient q0/2 - p^2/8 = 0. For that coefficient I checked that p = 2(A2/A0)(B2/B0) and q0 = p^2/4, and that terms of order r^k carry only frequencies up to k, so quarter-turn averaging leaves only degrees 0 and 1 below 3. Also the uniform transfer estimates and the exact Markov tower identity.
- Sec. 4: the reverse refresh identity (sign and normalization); the analytic flow majorant (derivative of the exponential weight gives -(d/8)Y); compression (M-1 <= (m-1)/2 for q >= 4, nesting 2q-1 <= L, carry factor L^2 e^{-d/2}); the triangular stable-graph recursion and its backward and forward sums; energy transversality via Z_k = J s_k^2 E0[E | boundary] and positive energy covariance; the sign and normalization of V_0; periodization; the marked-square coupling and its error sum.
- Sec. 5: the pivotal-passage lemma; the area exponent identity uv/b^2 (b/u)^{p4}(u/v)^{ph} v^{p1} = (b/u)^{p4-2}(u/v)^{ph-1} v^{p1}; the half-plane recursion q(u) <= e + C C0 K^{-1-c} q(C0 K u); the ring product bound; bootstrap order of choices; the dominated-convergence final sum.
- Sec. 6: the private-bit tree identity (only the empty and full selections survive, E[D^2] = 2 sech^2); finite-table margins; the strict-incidence Holley comparison; stopped reveals; the MTP2 rectangle identity and preservation under marginalization; the interior density proof with extreme ratio bounded by c^{-2}.
- Sec. 7: the boundary-squeeze incidence tables in both comparisons, including corridor angles relative to the marks and the plus/minus arcs; the conditioned-TV gluing; local redrawing; Rado continuity; strip selection and the slow diagonal; forbidden sides; the ordered-chords area argument; the progress-coordinate six-passage upgrade.
sibling_notes: The family-218 board already had entries for rank 67 (bulk correlations), rank 53 (the companion toolkit: buffered comparison, transmission, CLE resolution) and rank 92 (quenched random-bond SLE3), all marked no_gap_found. It mattered because this paper imports its pure inputs from the rank-53 companion, and that paper shares the charge identity and radial-gap computation with rank 67, where the identity had been checked numerically. I relied on those checks for the imported material and spent this audit on the new parts: the transfer/flow, edit stability, bit-representation comparison, and the boundary/curve arguments.
